newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Hana gets US$100 million.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Hana gets US$100 million.

text.p: Hana Bank launched a US$100 million floating rate note into Asian debt markets on Tuesday and bankers said more South Korean bank deals are on the way.

Hana's note issue matures in December 2001 but can be put or called on the third anniversary. The issue pays a coupon of 31.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 36.4 basis points.
Citicorp International and IBJ Asia are arrangers and bookrunners. Other arrangers are DKB Asia, Dresdner South East Asia and Banca Nazionale de Lavoro Singapore.

The notes are priced much more tightly than Hana's last FRN, which was launched in May and paid an all-in of 41 basis points. But that's hardly surprising given the trend in Korean bank paper this year, which has been toward tighter spreads.

Korean bank issues traded in the secondary market had seen spreads tighten in the run-up to South Korea's long-anticipated invitation to join the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, which was extended on October 11.
Traders said the narrower spreads recently have discouraged some potential buyers of Korean paper, so prices have been mostly steady lately.
"I think some potential buyers stayed away because spreads are too tight and there is not much benefit in (holding Korean paper)," said one trader.
"But we didnt see any huge selling, so I would say that the spreads are going to consolidate at current levels," he said.
Seoulbank has mandated SBC Warburg to arrange a US$100 million FRN, sources said Tuesday.
The three-year paper is expected to pay a margin of 44.5 basis points and an all-in return of 49 basis points.

SBC lead a 10-year callable FRN for Seoulbank in July. The bond paid 80 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries to the call and 200 basis points over the benchmark thereafter. Fees were 40 basis points.
In April, the bank tried a three-year FRN at 42 basis points all-in, but most bankers thought that spread extraordinarily skinny for Baa2-rated Seoulbank and the deal did not go well.
Bankers said several other Korean banks are looking for funding, including A3-rated Cho Hung Bank.

From Hong Kong came news that International Bank of Asia has mandated four banks to arrange a HK$500 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue, the latest in a long list of banks accessing the Hong Kong dollar market in the last quarter of this year.

Chase Manhattan will launch a HK$1.5 billion FRCD later this week or early next that is expected to be eligible for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Bankers said the LAF FRCDs for Dah Sing Bank and Bank of East Asia appear to be going well in syndication. Dao Heng Bank more recently launched a LAF issue.
